body:
This PR is step number (2b) of #6272. The objective is to rework open boundary conditions and elevate them as real components of the time-stepping rather than kernels hidden in `filL_halo_regions!` Every open boundary will carry its own storage and we define three new methods - `initialize_boundary_conditions!` sets the initial state at iteration 0. - `cache_boundary_conditions!` stores the state and the first interior value at the base of each stage: before every stage with AB2 and RK3, once per step with split Runge–Kutta, whose stages restart from tⁿ. - `step_boundary_conditions!` advances the state by one stage, right after its field is advanced and with the stage's Δt: - `NonhydrostaticModel`: in `step_prognostic_fields!`, before the pressure solve; - `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel`: after the velocity and the tracer updates; - `SplitExplicitFreeSurface`: once per barotropic substep; - `ShallowWaterModel`: after its AB2 and RK3 substeps. This PR also generalizes all the open boundary schemes, adding - `φᵇ`: the exterior state, i.e. the halo cell beyond an `Open` side, or the boundary face for a normal velocity. - `φ₁`: the first interior value next to it. Note that, following this PR, the performance of the open boundary conditions might decrease a bit, because we are adding kernels in the split-explicit free surface loops that is a latency bound loop (I will post here the pre and post performance on a representative benchmark). I envision bringing back the performance in subsequent PRs (it is probably very simple to embed the halo fills in the stepping kernels). I will open an issue with the plan to do so (I have already prepared it but do not want to start doing performance optimization on a cleanup...), so that who wants to pick up the challenge with an elegant solution can do it! For who is interested in the details, here there is a complete description, code and visualizations, of the complete open boundary conditions time stepping procedure with a hydrostatic model and a split explicit free surface
The whole walkthrough ## Open boundaries as time-stepped states: `HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel` + `SplitExplicitFreeSurface` One `SplitRungeKutta3` time step with `ObliqueRadiation` on the east side. Links point to 35cb83235. ```julia using Oceananigans using Oceananigans.BoundaryConditions: ObliqueRadiation, GravityWaveRadiationBoundaryCondition grid = RectilinearGrid(size = (64, 32, 16), x = (0, 400e3), y = (0, 200e3), z = (-1000, 0), topology = ((Closed, Open), Periodic, Bounded)) U_bcs = FieldBoundaryConditions(grid, (Face(), Center(), nothing); east = GravityWaveRadiationBoundaryCondition((0.0, 0.0))) # (Uᵉˣᵗ, ηᵉˣᵗ), η gets SurfaceWaveRadiation u_bcs = FieldBoundaryConditions(east = NormalFlowBoundaryCondition(0; scheme = ObliqueRadiation())) c_bcs = FieldBoundaryConditions(east = ValueBoundaryCondition(0; scheme = ObliqueRadiation())) model = HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModel(grid; free_surface = SplitExplicitFreeSurface(grid; substeps = 30), timestepper = :SplitRungeKutta3, tracers = :c, buoyancy = nothing, boundary_conditions = (U = U_bcs, u = u_bcs, c = c_bcs)) ``` ### 1. The exterior state ``` interior x = Lx exterior (halo) Nx-2 Nx-1 Nx Nx+1 Nx+2 ───┬─────────────┬─────────────┬─────────────╥─────────────┬─────────────┬── c, η │ o │ o │ o ║ X │ . │ ───┴─────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────╨─────────────┴─────────────┴── u, U o o o X . Nx-2 Nx-1 Nx Nx+1 Nx+2 o prognostic interior X exterior state φᵇ: one value per boundary point (j, k), stepped like the interior . not used ``` | `X` | scheme | set by | |:--|:--|:--| | `u[Nx+1, j, k]` | `ObliqueRadiation` | `step_boundary_conditions!` after `u` is advanced, then `correct_barotropic_mode!` | | `c[Nx+1, j, k]` | `ObliqueRadiation` | `step_boundary_conditions!` after `c` is advanced | | `η[Nx+1, j]` | `SurfaceWaveRadiation` (Chapman) | `step_boundary_conditions!`, every barotropic substep | | `U[Nx+1, j]` | `GravityWaveRadiation` (Flather) | halo fill, every barotropic substep | ### 2. Lifecycle of an exterior state ``` hook writes when (SplitRungeKutta3) ─────────────────────────────── ───────────────────────────────────────────── ─────────────────────────── initialize_boundary_conditions! c[Nx+1] ← c[Nx] (u[Nx+1] kept as set) iteration 0 cache_boundary_conditions! φᵇ[j, k] ← c[Nx+1], φ₁[j, k] ← c[Nx] once per step, at tⁿ step_boundary_conditions! c[Nx+1] ← F(φᵇ, φ₁, c[Nx], c[Nx-1], φᵉˣᵗ, Δτ) after c is advanced, every stage fill_halo_regions! nothing: c[Nx+1] stays in place every fill ``` [open_boundary_utils.jl#L88-L117](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/BoundaryConditions/open_boundary_schemes/open_boundary_utils.jl#L88-L117) ```julia @inline _fill_east_halo!(j, k, grid, c, ::RBC, loc, args...) = nothing # ... @kernel function _update_exterior_state!(update!, c, side, bc, loc, grid, args) i, j = @index(Global, NTuple) update!(side, i, j, grid, c, bc, loc, args...) end # ... step_boundary_condition!(bc::RBC, side, field, clock, model_fields, Δt) = update_exterior_state!(step_exterior_state!, bc, side, field, clock, model_fields, Δt) cache_boundary_condition!(bc::RBC, side, field, clock, model_fields) = update_exterior_state!(cache_exterior_state!, bc, side, field) initialize_boundary_condition!(bc::RBC, side, field, clock, model_fields) = update_exterior_state!(initialize_exterior_state!, bc, side, field, clock, model_fields) ``` ### 3. One time step ```mermaid flowchart TD C0["cache_current_fields!
cache_boundary_conditions!: φᵇ ← c[Nx+1], φ₁ ← c[Nx] at tⁿ"] subgraph ST["stage m = 1, 2, 3 — Δτ = Δt / βₘ"] V["rk_substep_velocities!: u = uⁿ + Δτ Gᵘ
step_boundary_conditions!(u) → u[Nx+1]"] subgraph BT["barotropic substep — Δτᴮ"] B1["cache_boundary_conditions!(η): φᵇ ← η[Nx+1]"] B2["U, V kernel"] B3["fill U → U[Nx+1] (Flather)"] B4["pin_barotropic_faces! (target_transport)"] B5["η kernel, reads U[Nx+1]"] B6["step_boundary_conditions!(η) → η[Nx+1] (Chapman)"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> B6 end A["η, U ← η̅, U̅
refill U → U[Nx+1] (Flather)"] I["correct_barotropic_mode!
u[Nx+1] += (U − Σₖ Δz u) / H"] T["rk_substep_tracers!: c = cⁿ + Δτ Gᶜ
step_boundary_conditions!(c) → c[Nx+1]"] K["update_state!
fill_halo_regions! leaves c[Nx+1]"] V --> B1 B6 -->|next substep| B1 B6 --> A --> I --> T --> K end C0 --> V K -->|next stage| V ``` Every stage restarts from the cache at `tⁿ`: ``` cache φᵇ, φ₁ at tⁿ stage 1 tⁿ ─────────────────> tⁿ + Δt/3 stage 2 tⁿ ─────────────────────────────> tⁿ + Δt/2 stage 3 tⁿ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────> tⁿ + Δt ``` With `QuasiAdamsBashforth2` and `RungeKutta3` the cache runs before every stage instead. [split_runge_kutta.jl#L174](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/TimeSteppers/split_runge_kutta.jl#L174), [hydrostatic_free_surface_rk_step.jl#L161](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/Models/HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModels/hydrostatic_free_surface_rk_step.jl#L161), [#L217](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/Models/HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModels/hydrostatic_free_surface_rk_step.jl#L217) ```julia cache_current_fields!(model) cache_boundary_conditions!(model) # ... rk_substep_velocities! add_barotropic_acceleration!(velocities, model.grid, model.free_surface, ηⁿ, -Δt) step_boundary_conditions!(velocities, model.clock, fields(model), Δt) # ... rk_substep_tracers! foreach_name(tracers) do val_tracer_index, val_tracer_name rk_substep_tracer!(model, Δt, val_tracer_index, val_tracer_name) end step_boundary_conditions!(tracers, model.clock, fields(model), Δt) ``` ### 4. One boundary point The kernel runs on the boundary plane, so `(i, j)` in `step_exterior_state!` is `(j, k)` on the east side. Shown for `c`; for `u` the stencil moves half a cell left and `Uᵃ = u[Nx]` itself. ``` φ₂ⁿ⁺¹ φ₁ⁿ⁺¹ φᵇⁿ⁺¹ c[Nx-1] c[Nx] c[Nx+1] ───┬─────────────┬─────────────╥─────────────┬── │ R │ R ║ W │ ───┴─────────────┴─────────────╨─────────────┴── R u[Nx] = Uᵃ (u[Nx+1] with use_boundary_velocity = true) cache: φᵇ[j, k] = φᵇⁿ, φ₁[j, k] = φ₁ⁿ exterior data: φᵉˣᵗ = getbc(bc, j, k, grid, clock, model_fields) ``` [normal_radiation.jl#L143-L174](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/BoundaryConditions/open_boundary_schemes/normal_radiation.jl#L143-L174) ```julia @inline function cache_exterior_state!(side, i, j, grid, c, bc::ORBC, loc) iᵇ, jᵇ, kᵇ = boundary_point(side, loc, grid, 0, i, j) i₁, j₁, k₁ = boundary_point(side, loc, grid, 1, i, j) radiation = bc.classification.scheme @inbounds radiation.φᵇ[i, j] = c[iᵇ, jᵇ, kᵇ] @inbounds radiation.φ₁[i, j] = c[i₁, j₁, k₁] return nothing end # A convex combination of the boundary value at the base of the stage, the interior and the exterior value, so it is bounded @inline function step_exterior_state!(side, i, j, grid, c, bc::ORBC, loc, clock, model_fields, Δt) iᵇ, jᵇ, kᵇ = boundary_point(side, loc, grid, 0, i, j) i₁, j₁, k₁ = boundary_point(side, loc, grid, 1, i, j) i₂, j₂, k₂ = boundary_point(side, loc, grid, 2, i, j) radiation = bc.classification.scheme @inbounds begin φᵉˣᵗ = getbc(bc, i, j, grid, clock, model_fields) φ₁ⁿ⁺¹ = c[i₁, j₁, k₁] φ₂ⁿ⁺¹ = c[i₂, j₂, k₂] n = ifelse(radiation.use_boundary_velocity, 0, 1) Uᵃ = advecting_velocity(bc, side, model_fields, grid, n, i, j, φ₁ⁿ⁺¹) Cᵃ = abs(Uᵃ) * Δt * reciprocal_boundary_spacing(side, grid, i, j) outflow = outward(side, Uᵃ) >= 0 φᵇⁿ⁺¹ = radiation_update(radiation, side, i, j, radiation.φᵇ[i, j], φ₁ⁿ⁺¹, φ₂ⁿ⁺¹, radiation.φ₁[i, j], φᵉˣᵗ, Δt, outflow, Cᵃ) c[iᵇ, jᵇ, kᵇ] = ifelse(immersed_boundary_point(side, loc, grid, i, j), zero(grid), φᵇⁿ⁺¹) end return nothing end ``` ### 5. The oblique part The tangential neighbours come from the cache, which no thread writes during the step: ``` field c φ₁[:, k] φᵇ[:, k] cache at tⁿ cache at tⁿ Nx-1 Nx Nx+1 ┌───────┬───────╥───────┐ ┌───────┐ ┌───────┐ j+1 │ │ ║ │ │ R │ │ R │ ├───────┼───────╫───────┤ ├───────┤ ├───────┤ j │ R │ R ║ W │ │ R │ │ R │ ├───────┼───────╫───────┤ ├───────┤ ├───────┤ j-1 │ │ ║ │ │ R │ │ R │ └───────┴───────╨───────┘ └───────┘ └───────┘ normal, implicit upwind: φ₁ⁿ⁺¹ ───Cₙ───> φᵇⁿ⁺¹ <───Δt/τ─── φᵉˣᵗ tangential, explicit upwind: φᵇ[j-1] ───Cₜ > 0───> φᵇ[j] <───Cₜ < 0─── φᵇ[j+1] ``` [oblique_radiation.jl#L98-L122](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/BoundaryConditions/open_boundary_schemes/oblique_radiation.jl#L98-L122) ```julia @inline function oblique_radiation_update(φᵇⁿ, φ₁ⁿ⁺¹, φ₂ⁿ⁺¹, φ₁ⁿ, δᵇ₋, δᵇ₊, δ₁₋, δ₁₊, φᵉˣᵗ, Δt, radiation, outflow, Cᵃ) ∂t_φ = φ₁ⁿ⁺¹ - φ₁ⁿ ∂ξ_φ = φ₁ⁿ⁺¹ - φ₂ⁿ⁺¹ ∂η_φ = ifelse(-∂t_φ * (δ₁₋ + δ₁₊) > 0, δ₁₋, δ₁₊) FT = typeof(∂ξ_φ) D = max(∂ξ_φ^2 + ∂η_φ^2, eps(FT)) Cᶜ = - ∂t_φ * ∂ξ_φ / D Cₙ = ifelse(outflow, max(zero(FT), min(one(FT), max(Cᶜ, Cᵃ))), zero(FT)) Cₜ = ifelse(outflow, clamp(- ∂t_φ * ∂η_φ / D, -one(FT), one(FT)), zero(FT)) τ = ifelse(outflow, radiation.outflow_timescale, radiation.inflow_timescale) τ̃ = Δt / τ φᵇⁿ⁺¹ = (φᵇⁿ + Cₙ * φ₁ⁿ⁺¹ - max(Cₜ, zero(FT)) * δᵇ₋ - min(Cₜ, zero(FT)) * δᵇ₊ + τ̃ * φᵉˣᵗ) / (1 + Cₙ + τ̃) return ifelse(τ == 0, φᵉˣᵗ, φᵇⁿ⁺¹) end # The tangential derivatives are those of the boundary and interior values at the base of the stage @inline function radiation_update(radiation::ObliqueRadiation, ::Union{West, East, South, North}, i, j, φᵇⁿ, φ₁ⁿ⁺¹, φ₂ⁿ⁺¹, φ₁ⁿ, φᵉˣᵗ, Δt, outflow, Cᵃ) δᵇ₋, δᵇ₊ = tangential_differences(radiation.φᵇ, i, j) δ₁₋, δ₁₊ = tangential_differences(radiation.φ₁, i, j) return oblique_radiation_update(φᵇⁿ, φ₁ⁿ⁺¹, φ₂ⁿ⁺¹, φ₁ⁿ, δᵇ₋, δᵇ₊, δ₁₋, δ₁₊, φᵉˣᵗ, Δt, radiation, outflow, Cᵃ) end ``` Outflow: `Cₙ = clamp(max(Cᶜ, Cᵃ), 0, 1)`, `Cₜ ∈ [-1, 1]`, `τ = outflow_timescale`. Inflow: `Cₙ = Cₜ = 0`, `τ = inflow_timescale` (default `0`, so `φᵇⁿ⁺¹ = φᵉˣᵗ`). ### 6. Barotropic boundary, every substep ``` η[Nx-1] η[Nx] η[Nx+1] ───┬─────────────┬─────────────╥─────────────┬── │ o │ o ║ X │ ───┴─────────────┴─────────────╨─────────────┴── o X U[Nx] U[Nx+1] cache φᵇ ← η[Nx+1] fill U[Nx+1] ← Uᵉˣᵗ + √(gH) ((η[Nx] + η[Nx+1]) / 2 − ηᵉˣᵗ) Flather pin U[Nx+1, :] −= (Σⱼ Δy U[Nx+1, j] − target) / Σⱼ Δy target_transport only η η[Nx] += Δτᴮ (F − ∇·U) step η[Nx+1] ← (φᵇ + C η[Nx]) / (1 + C), C = √(gH) Δτᴮ / Δx Chapman ``` [step_split_explicit_free_surface.jl#L145-L162](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/Models/HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModels/SplitExplicitFreeSurfaces/step_split_explicit_free_surface.jl#L145-L162) ```julia @unroll for substep in 1:Nsubsteps @inbounds averaging_weight = weights[substep] @inbounds transport_weight = transport_weights[substep] substep_clock = (; time = add_time_interval(clock.time, Δτᴮ, substep - 1), iteration = clock.iteration, stage = 0, last_stage_Δt = Δτᴮ) only_local_halos = substep == 1 || (substep - 1) % exchange_interval != 0 maybe_distributed_fill_halo_regions!(arch, η_halo_args[1:end-1]..., substep_clock, η_halo_args[end]; only_local_halos) @apply_regionally cache_boundary_conditions!((U, V, η), substep_clock, barotropic_model_fields) @apply_regionally apply_barotropic_kernel!(velocity_kernel!, transport_weight, converted_U_args) @apply_regionally step_boundary_conditions!((U, V), substep_clock, barotropic_model_fields, Δτᴮ) maybe_distributed_fill_halo_regions!(arch, U_halo_args[1:end-1]..., substep_clock, U_halo_args[end]; only_local_halos) maybe_distributed_fill_halo_regions!(arch, V_halo_args[1:end-1]..., substep_clock, V_halo_args[end]; only_local_halos) pin_barotropic_faces!(face_pins) @apply_regionally apply_barotropic_kernel!(free_surface_kernel!, averaging_weight, converted_η_args) @apply_regionally step_boundary_conditions!((η,), substep_clock, barotropic_model_fields, Δτᴮ) end ``` [gravity_wave_schemes.jl#L306-L319](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/BoundaryConditions/open_boundary_schemes/gravity_wave_schemes.jl#L306-L319) ```julia @inline function step_exterior_state!(side::Union{West, East, South, North}, i, j, grid, η, bc::IGWVBC, loc, clock, model_fields, Δt) iᵇ, jᵇ, kᵇ = boundary_point(side, loc, grid, 0, i, j) i₁, j₁, k₁ = boundary_point(side, loc, grid, 1, i, j) g = bc.classification.scheme.gravitational_acceleration @inbounds begin η₁ = η[i₁, j₁, k₁] H = column_depthᶜᶜᵃ(i₁, j₁, k₁, grid, η) C = sqrt(g * max(H, zero(H))) * Δt * reciprocal_boundary_spacing(side, grid, i, j) η[iᵇ, jᵇ, kᵇ] = (bc.classification.scheme.φᵇ[i, j] + C * η₁) / (1 + C) end return nothing end ``` ### 7. `u[Nx+1]` carries the Flather transport `correct_barotropic_mode!` runs on `i ∈ -Hx+2:Nx+Hx-1`, boundary face included ([barotropic_split_explicit_corrector.jl#L62-L68](https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/blob/35cb8323535a7d07f7923a8f1b1f723073ead099/src/Models/HydrostaticFreeSurfaceModels/SplitExplicitFreeSurfaces/barotropic_split_explicit_corrector.jl#L62-L68)): ``` after step_boundary_conditions!(u) after correct_barotropic_mode! k = Nz u★[Nx+1, j, Nz] u★[Nx+1, j, Nz] + δ ... ... ... k = 1 u★[Nx+1, j, 1] u★[Nx+1, j, 1] + δ δ = (U[Nx+1, j] − Σₖ Δzₖ u★[Nx+1, j, k]) / H ⇒ Σₖ Δzₖ u[Nx+1, j, k] = U[Nx+1, j] ObliqueRadiation: vertical structure Flather: depth integral ```

title: Rework open boundaries

body:
Since #6312, the substep loop for split-explicit free surfaces that fill halos sets

```julia
only_local_halos = substep == 1 || (substep - 1) % exchange_interval != 0
```

Extended halos start the substeps filled, so skipping the exchange before the first substep is fine for them. `CompleteHaloFilling` (`extend_halos = false`) has `exchange_interval = 1` and, before #6312, exchanged before every substep. Now it skips the first one, so the rank seams start each barotropic step from stale halos and distributed runs differ from serial.

This PR restores the exchange before the first substep for `CompleteHaloFilling` only, and leaves extended halos as they are:

```julia
@inline exchange_halos(free_surface, substep, exchange_interval) = substep > 1 && (substep - 1) % exchange_interval == 0
@inline exchange_halos(::SplitExplicitFreeSurface{CompleteHaloFilling}, substep, exchange_interval) = true
```

The existing testset "Distributed open boundary conditions" in `test/mpi/split_explicit_boundaries.jl` catches this: on `main` it fails for `extend_halos = false` (`u`, `v` and `η` differ from serial), and it passes with this change. The distributed tests run on the separate Buildkite distributed pipeline, which does not report a status on `main` commits, so the failure went unnoticed.

## Tests

- `test/mpi/split_explicit_boundaries.jl` on 4 ranks, CPU and 4 GPUs: "Distributed open boundary conditions" fails on `main` (CPU) and passes with this change; the full file passes with this change
- serial `hydrostatic_free_surface/split_explicit_boundaries.jl`, `split_explicit_solver.jl` and `open_boundary_conditions.jl` on CPU: pass

title: Exchange the barotropic halos before the first substep with `CompleteHaloFilling`

body:
Resolves #6390.

An operation is computed from its operands, and a `FunctionField` from its function, so neither has state of its own or needs to be checkpointed. This PR tells the checkpointer that, the same way `ZeroField`, `OneField` and `ConstantField` already do:

```julia
prognostic_state(::AbstractOperation) = nothing
prognostic_state(::FunctionField) = nothing
```
title: Fix pickup when `auxiliary_fields` include an `AbstractOperation` or `FunctionField`

body:
`Adapt.adapt_structure` for `AdaptiveVerticallyImplicitDiscretization` passed `cfl` and `Δt[]` through without calling `adapt`:

```julia
AdaptiveVerticallyImplicitDiscretization(a.cfl, a.Δt[])
```

Under Reactant, `Δt` is a `Ref` holding a traced number, which has to be converted by Reactant's kernel adaptor before the struct goes into a kernel. Because it wasn't, any kernel that reads `td.Δt` fails to compile (`InvalidIRError`, on both the CPU and GPU Reactant backends). A downstream calibration harness built on Breeze's single-column mode currently needs a local `adapt_structure` override to get correct forward values and gradients.

The fix passes both fields through `Adapt.adapt(to, ...)`. For plain floats on CPU and CUDA, this changes nothing.

Tests:
- `test/reactant/unit.jl`: compiles a kernel that writes a traced `td.Δt` into a field. It fails before the fix and passes after.
- `test/unit/adaptive_implicit_vertical_advection.jl`: a test adaptor that converts `Float64` to `Float32` checks that both fields are adapted, and checks that `adapt(Array, td)` leaves the values unchanged.

title: Adapt the fields of AdaptiveVerticallyImplicitDiscretization for kernels

body:
The `RungeKutta3TimeStepper` docstring cites Le and Moin (1991), who use Crank–Nicolson for the implicit terms in each substep. Oceananigans instead uses backward Euler over each substep `Δτ = Δt * (γᵐ + ζᵐ)`, which is L-stable (important for stiff vertical mixing and adaptive-implicit advection) but first-order accurate in time for the implicit part. This PR adds a sentence to the docstring saying so.

Docstring-only change.

title: Document that RungeKutta3TimeStepper treats implicit terms with backward Euler
